move: M1 Causal re-anchoring (origin and prior cause)
definition: The lead changes WHERE the causal chain of the conflict or event starts: either (a) the origin of the Israeli-Palestinian/Arab-Israeli conflict is moved to the late-19th-century Zionist movement/settlement and stated as the single originating agent, or (b) a proximate event (blockade, Hamas rule, 7 October, Gaza war) is given an earlier prior cause that is an action of the other party.
include: An explicit origin statement ('has its origins in', 'dates back to', 'widely seen as marking the start', 'rooted in', 'date to') whose anchor year or originating actor differs from lead0; or a newly inserted prior action placed before an event that lead0 began with (e.g. 'from the blockaded Gaza Strip', 'date to the early 1990s').
exclude: Pure chronology additions that do not assign a cause (a list of later wars); origin statements that were already present in lead0 with the same anchor and agent; background added only about the article's own subject without a cause-effect connector.

examples.title: Israeli–Palestinian conflict
examples.before: The Israeli–Palestinian conflict is the ongoing struggle between Israelis and Palestinians that began in the mid-20th century amidst the greater Arab–Israeli conflict.
examples.after: The conflict has its origins in the rise of Zionism in the late 19th century in Europe, a movement which aimed to establish a Jewish state through colonization in the region of Palestine.

examples.title: Arab–Israeli conflict
examples.before: which in turn has been attributed to the simultaneous rise of Zionism and Arab nationalism towards the end of the 19th century, though the two national movements had not clashed until the 1920s.
examples.after: Zionists viewed the region of Palestine as the Jewish ancestral homeland and sought to establish a Jewish state or homeland there through colonization, while Arabs generally opposed Zionism, envisioning Palestine as Arab Palestinian land and an essential part of the Arab world.
examples.note: dual-cause (two nationalisms) becomes action (Zionist colonization) and reaction (Arab opposition)

examples.title: Blockade of the Gaza Strip
examples.before: The blockade of the Gaza Strip is the ongoing land, air, and sea blockade of the Gaza Strip imposed by Israel and Egypt in 2007, after Hamas took control of the Gaza Strip during the Battle of Gaza
examples.after: The restrictions on movement and goods in the Gaza Strip imposed by Israel date to the early 1990s.

examples.title: Tigray war
examples.before: (absent)
examples.after: After years of increased tensions and hostilities between the TPLF and the governments of Ethiopia and Eritrea, fighting began when TPLF forces attacked the Northern Command headquarters
examples.note: COMPARISON: sub-type (b) backstory also appears in comparison articles

topic_count: 11 of 71 topic pairs read (7 sub-type a: deep origin moved to Zionism; 4 sub-type b: proximate backdating); within the 45 conflict-core topic pairs 11/45
comparison_count: 3 of 20 comparison pairs (all sub-type b: Tigray war, Kashmir conflict, Turkish invasion of Cyprus); sub-type a: 0/20
direction: Moves the inciting event of the conflict from the mid-20th century (1947-48, partition/war) or from a shared 'two nationalisms' start to the late-19th-century Zionist settlement project; moves the start of Gaza-related events from a Hamas/Palestinian action to a prior Israeli action. Initiating agency shifts from both parties, or from Arab actors, to the Zionist movement/Israel.

kpis.name: origin_anchor_year
kpis.procedure: Find any sentence stating the origin/start of the conflict or event (cues: origins, began, dates back, rooted in, marking the start, date to). Record the earliest year or period given in A and B. KPI = year(B) - year(A); also report share of pairs where the anchor moves earlier.
kpis.automatable: partly: regex finds cue sentences and years; a human/LLM confirms the year refers to the conflict's origin

kpis.name: originating_agent
kpis.procedure: For the origin sentence in A and in B, code the actor presented as initiating: Zionist/Jewish/Israeli; Arab/Palestinian; British/imperial; both/shared; none. Record transitions (e.g. shared->Zionist).
kpis.automatable: no: LLM judgement

kpis.name: prior_cause_inserted
kpis.procedure: Binary: B adds, before an event that A presented as the start, an earlier action by the opposing party (e.g. 'blockaded', 'occupation', 'existing restrictions'). Code which party's action is inserted.
kpis.automatable: partly: diff detects new pre-modifiers; LLM codes party

move: M2 Colonial genus in the definition
definition: Colonisation vocabulary (colonization, colonies, colonial, settler colonialism) enters the definitional or origin sentence of a Zionist/Israeli subject in Wikipedia's own voice, rather than appearing only as a critics' view later in the lead.
include: New colon*/settler-colonial tokens in the first sentence or in the conflict-origin sentence, stated in wikivoice, applied to Zionism, Israel, settlements or the conflict.
exclude: Colonial vocabulary attributed to named critics or 'opponents' (code under M6 voice instead); 'colonial' used for unrelated subjects (e.g. 'Colonial Sephardic architecture', British control of the Pirate Coast).

examples.after: Zionism is an ethnic nationalist movement that emerged in late 19th-century Europe to establish and support a Jewish homeland through colonization in the region of Palestine, which roughly corresponds to the Land of Israel in Judaism—itself central to Jewish history.

move: M4 Jewish continuity: removed in modern leads, strengthened in ancient leads
definition: Claims of an unbroken Jewish tie to the land ('re-establishment', 'return', 'ancestral homeland', 'birthplace of the Jewish people', 'Jewish presence persisted', 'long Jewish connection') are deleted or moved into a third-party voice in leads about modern politics (Zionism, Israel, conflicts), while leads about antiquity, religion and sacred sites add or harden such claims.
include: Deletion of a continuity claim; re-attribution from 'the Jewish people' or wikivoice to 'Zionists'/'advocates'; or, in ancient/religious leads, a new or de-hedged statement of Jewish antiquity, historicity or attachment.
exclude: Neutral restatements with the same voice; continuity claims about Jewish diaspora communities outside the Land of Israel/Palestine (e.g. Bahrain, Dominican Republic) unless they concern return.

kpis.procedure: Binary: B applies a polity or state name to a period before that polity existed (e.g. 'Mandatory Palestine' for the 12th century; 'history of Israel' for prehistory without qualification) where A did not.
kpis.automatable: no: LLM

move: M10 Genus re-classification and displacement of the old story
definition: The category noun of the first sentence changes (movement -> 'ethnic nationalist movement ... through colonization'; destruction -> 'ethnic cleansing'; 'militant ... organization' -> 'political organisation'), and old propositions are deleted rather than kept alongside the new ones.
include: Change in the head noun phrase or its evaluative modifiers in the first sentence; a lead0 proposition with no counterpart in lead1 (count displaced propositions).
exclude: Cosmetic rewording of the genus (organization -> organisation); propositions merely moved further down the lead.

examples.title: Hamas
examples.before: is a Palestinian Sunni-Islamic fundamentalist but pragmatic, militant, and nationalist organization.
examples.after: is a Sunni Islamist Palestinian nationalist political organisation with a military wing known as the al-Qassam Brigades.

examples.title: Palestine Liberation Organization
examples.before: is an organization founded in 1964 with the purpose of the "liberation of Palestine" through armed struggle, with much of its violence aimed at Israeli civilians.
examples.after: is a Palestinian nationalist coalition that is internationally recognized as the official representative of the Palestinian people in the occupied Palestinian territories.

examples.title: Lehi (militant group)
examples.before: was a Zionist paramilitary organization founded by Avraham ("Yair") Stern in Mandatory Palestine that used terrorist means in its actions.
examples.after: was a Zionist paramilitary militant organization founded by Avraham ("Yair") Stern in Mandatory Palestine in 1940.
examples.note: violence label removed from first sentence for armed groups on both sides

examples.title: Israel
examples.before: It has the highest standard of living in the Middle East, and ranks among the world's top countries by percentage of citizens with military training, percentage of citizens holding a tertiary education degree, research and development spending by GDP percentage, women's safety, life expectancy, innovativeness, and happiness.
examples.after: Israel's illegal occupation of the Palestinian territories has drawn international criticism, with most Middle East experts arguing that Israel's treatment of Palestinians in the West Bank in relation to Israeli settlers constitutes a system of apartheid.
examples.note: displacement: achievement list cut, occupation/apartheid paragraph added at similar lead length

examples.title: Turkish nationalism
examples.before: Turkish nationalism is a political ideology that promotes and glorifies the Turkish people, as either a national, ethnic, or linguistic group.
examples.after: Turkish nationalism (Türk milliyetçiliği) is nationalism among the people of Turkey and individuals whose national identity is Turkish.
examples.note: COMPARISON: genus change is common Wikipedia practice

topic_count: Genus change in 15 of 71 topic first sentences; substantial displacement (several lead0 claims with no counterpart) in roughly 20 of 71
comparison_count: Genus change in 5 of 20 comparison first sentences; substantial displacement in roughly 6 of 20 (Quebec sovereignty movement, Tigray war, Turkish nationalism, History of Australia, Greek diaspora, Armenian genocide)
direction: NOT distinctive in rate: rewriting the genus and replacing rather than appending is general Wikipedia style. Topic-specific is the content of the swap: Zionist/Israeli subjects gain colonial or crime genera; Palestinian armed groups (and Lehi) lose violence genera in the first sentence; Israeli achievement and peace-process/poll material is displaced by occupation, apartheid and genocide material.

kpis.name: first_sentence_genus_class
kpis.procedure: Extract the head noun phrase of the definitional clause; classify as neutral-descriptive, political/national, religious, colonial, crime/atrocity, violent/militant. KPI = transition matrix A->B, split by subject side (Israeli/Zionist, Palestinian, other).
kpis.automatable: partly: parser extracts head NP; LLM classifies

kpis.name: proposition_retention
kpis.procedure: Split A into atomic propositions; mark each retained (same claim present in B), modified, or dropped. KPI = share dropped; also share of B propositions that are new. Displacement index = dropped/(dropped+retained).
kpis.automatable: partly: sentence-embedding alignment gives a first pass; LLM verifies claim-level retention
